claim: With server-side encryption for a Kinesis data stream that is the Firehose source, Kinesis Data Streams encrypts the data with an AWS KMS key before storing it at rest, and when the Firehose stream reads the data, Kinesis Data Streams first decrypts it and then sends it to Firehose. Firehose buffers the data in memory and delivers it to the destinations without storing the unencrypted data at rest.

qualifiers.scope: Kinesis data stream as source, with Kinesis Data Streams server-side encryption

evidence.quote: When your Firehose stream reads the data from your data stream, Kinesis Data Streams first decrypts the data and then sends it to Amazon Data Firehose. Amazon Data Firehose buffers the data in memory based on the buffering hints that you specify. It then delivers it to your destinations without storing the unencrypted data at rest.
When you send data from your data producers to your data stream, Kinesis Data Streams encrypts your data using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key before storing the data at rest.

For information about how to enable server-side encryption for Kinesis Data Streams, see [Using Server-Side Encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/server-side-encryption.html) in the *Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Developer Guide*.
